name: Separator
description: Pure-CSS horizontal or vertical separator: solid, dashed, dotted or faded, with a centered (“or”) or aligned label, on <hr> or <div>.
useWhen: Two groups of content or controls need a quiet visual split, horizontal or vertical
Alternative paths need a labeled divider, such as “or” between social login and email
A feed or timeline needs inline labels like Today between groups of items

avoidWhen.when: Spacing alone already separates the groups clearly and extra lines would add clutter
Sections need collapsible headings rather than a static line

classes.name: mv-separator
classes.description: On <hr> (horizontal) or <div>. If the element contains text or an icon, it becomes a labeled divider (line, label, line). Without a label, it must be strictly empty (no whitespace).

attributes.name: data-orientation
attributes.description: Vertical line; stretches to the height of the flex parent (min. 1em).

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: Line style; fade tapers off at the ends.

cssVars.name: --mv-separator-spacing
cssVars.description: Spacing on either side of the line.

a11y: <hr> already has role=separator. For a semantic <div>: role="separator" + aria-orientation="vertical" when vertical. Purely decorative: role="none" (or aria-hidden="true"). With a label (“or”, “Today”), don’t set role=separator (its children would become presentational): keep a plain <div> so the text is read.
